89	### Keep child branches linear — it decides how painful the merge is
90	
91	When a parent branch gains commits after its child was cut, **rebase the child onto the parent** (the child is unpushed or yours alone) rather than merging the parent in. Stack 03 learned this the expensive way; see below.
92	
93	### Merging a stack — what actually happens (learned 2026-09-17, twice)
94	
95	**`gh pr merge` refuses a stacked pull request**, and on the top of a stack it silently merges into the parent branch instead of `main`. Never use it on a stack. Merge **bottom-up** through the async route; `plans/scripts/land.sh <pr> "<title>" <message-file>` does the waiting and polling:
96	
97	```bash
98	gh api -X PUT repos/kgang/katalyst/pulls/<n>/merge-async -f merge_method=squash \
99	  -f commit_title="<subject> (#<n>)" -f commit_message="<the What, as prose>" -f sha=<head sha>
100	gh api repos/kgang/katalyst/pulls/<n>/merge-async/<uuid>      # poll until "merged"
101	```
102	
103	After a parent merges:
104	
105	1. **A linear child is restacked by GitHub itself** within about half a minute: rebased onto `main`, base retargeted to `main`. Your local copy of that branch is now behind a rewritten remote — check the trees are identical (`git diff --quiet origin/<b> <b>`) and `git reset --hard origin/<b>`. Then wait for checks and merge.
106	2. **A child carrying merge commits is not restacked.** Two cases:
107	   - *It is a strict superset of `main`* (it merged its parents in as they were first written). Prove it — the merged pull requests' original tips are ancestors, and `git diff --stat origin/main HEAD` lists only this pull request's files. A plain `git merge origin/main` will conflict on every file both sides touched (add/add against the squashed copies), so record the merge with `git merge -s ours origin/main`, confirm the tree did not change, push, `gh pr edit <n> --base main`.

148	## 8. Lessons — read these twice
149	
150	1. **After any interruption, check reality before acting.** `git log --oneline -5`, `git status`, `git worktree list`, `gh pr list`, and `STATUS.md`. Do not trust your memory of the repo; trust the repo.
151	2. **Append to `STATUS.md` before you stop**, and whenever the set of open pull requests or running agents changes. Record Kent's instructions there in his own words.
152	3. **Brief sub-agents fully, and point at the one copy.** They know only what you tell them. Give the plan and the decisions note by **absolute path in the main checkout** (readable from any worktree) rather than pasting tables — no transcription drift. Paste only what must be word for word on screen.
153	4. **Keep cross-references consistent.** After any rename or any changed number, search the whole repo. A fixture change in stack 03 made numbers stale in eight chapters, the PRD, a decision record and an end-to-end test.
154	5. **Whoever changes a fixture or an engine rule lists which chapter numbers went stale, and the sweep travels in the same pull request.** Resume the chapter's own writer for the sweep.
155	6. **Verify every sub-agent's claim yourself.** Run the tests and lints, read the diff against the owned-files list, hand-check arithmetic on a tiny map of your own, **launch the app and look**. A report is a hypothesis. In stack 03 this caught: a lint failure an agent reported as green, a plate overlap on a map the agent had not probed, and a fixed-height tile full of dead space.
156	7. **Write the shapes sheet before parallel writers start** — and for parallel stacks, the event or type vocabulary they share.
157	8. **Put a read-only reviewer over parallel writers, every time.** It found about ten blocking cross-chapter disagreements per stack — two names for one type, the same test named two ways, "six options" over a list of five, a block of invented numbers. Have it **re-do every worked number by hand from the fixture**.
158	9. **Two honest principles settle most small questions**: one rule over two (find the rule the code already obeys and name it once); and a code, a word or a number must mean what it says (that is why there is `edit_not_applicable`, why `killed` means only forced false, why the chip says "stated range · not computed").
159	10. **Never put a typed-in number where a computed one belongs — including in tests.** Assert directions, orderings and states; or compare a value with itself across a change.
160	11. **Property tests must build their inputs.** One that `assume()`s most inputs away fails Hypothesis's health check in CI on a bad seed while passing locally. CI is about 2.5× slower than this machine.
161	12. **The first pull request of a stack is small enough to write yourself**: commit chapter *stubs* (headings only) so code agents can branch off the spec branch at once.
162	13. **Opus agents can hit a session limit** ("resets 7am America/New_York"). If one dies, check disk state before reviving it by message.
163	15. **A client library accepting a shape proves nothing about the service.** In stack 04 the SDK built a schema from a union of three shapes without complaint and the service refused it on the first live call (`For 'anyOf', '$defs' is not supported`). Only a live call settles a vendor question — make the first one early, make it small, and do not close a chapter's open question on the library's say-so.
164	16. **Test a program as a program, and make a paid run impossible to lose.** Twice in stack 04 a run that cost money kept nothing: once because the recorder threw the receipt away with a file it would not write, once because the module's `__main__` guard sat above a function it called — invisible to every test (tests import, so everything is defined first) and to ruff and mypy. Run each `python -m` entry point in a subprocess test through its whole path; keep anything paid for incrementally, so a crash still leaves a file.
165	17. **A rare test failure is a bug until the evidence says otherwise.** Four times in stack 04 an agent's first instinct was "flaky — clear the example database": the keyboard left behind on a rebuilt tile; two keys in one frame; a locality leak through the day grid (a claim in a separate piece of the map moved by `.096`); a second through one global survival mask (`.083`). Every one was a real defect a user could hit. Find the falsifying input, rebuild it by hand, and decide with evidence whether the test or the product is wrong. And pytest TRUNCATES a repr — `Belief(p=1.85...` is `1.85e-05`, not a likelihood above 1.
166	18. **Several worktrees on one machine share one set of end-to-end ports.** Until stack 04 fixed it, `frontend/playwright.config.ts` used fixed ports and reused any server already up, so one agent's `npx playwright test` silently tested another branch's app — and "verified" numbers were wrong in both directions. Give every agent, and yourself, explicit ports (`KATALYST_E2E_BACKEND_PORT`, `KATALYST_E2E_FRONTEND_PORT`), never reuse a server, and never edit a source file under a running dev server (a hot reload blanks the page mid-test and looks like your change broke everything).
167	14. **Say what you merged and why before Kent has to ask**, and if you take a step earlier than he literally asked (stack 03a was merged while 03b's last pull request was still being built), tell him plainly and offer to hold.

1	#!/bin/bash
2	# land.sh <pr> <title> <message-file>
3	# GitHub restacks a child branch onto main by itself when its parent merges, so this only:
4	# checks the base is main and the branch sits on main, waits for the four checks, squash-merges via the async route.
5	set -euo pipefail
6	PR=$1; TITLE=$2; MSG=$3
7	cd /Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst
8	for i in $(seq 1 12); do BASE=$(gh pr view $PR --json baseRefName -q .baseRefName); [ "$BASE" = "main" ] && break; sleep 5; done
9	[ "$BASE" = "main" ] || { echo "base is $BASE, not main"; exit 3; }
10	git fetch -q origin
11	HEAD_SHA=$(gh pr view $PR --json headRefOid -q .headRefOid)
12	git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/main $HEAD_SHA || { echo "head $HEAD_SHA does not sit on main yet"; exit 5; }
13	echo "head ${HEAD_SHA:0:7} sits on main; waiting for checks…"
14	for i in $(seq 1 90); do
15	  out=$(gh pr checks $PR 2>&1 || true)
16	  if echo "$out" | grep -qw "fail"; then echo "CHECK FAILED:"; echo "$out"; exit 4; fi
17	  if ! echo "$out" | grep -qw "pending" && [ "$(echo "$out" | grep -cw pass)" -ge 4 ]; then break; fi
18	  sleep 10
19	done
20	gh pr checks $PR | awk '{print $1"="$2}' | tr '\n' ' '; echo
21	[ "$(gh pr view $PR --json headRefOid -q .headRefOid)" = "$HEAD_SHA" ] || { echo "head moved while waiting"; exit 6; }
22	R=$(gh api -X PUT repos/kgang/katalyst/pulls/$PR/merge-async -f merge_method=squash -f commit_title="$TITLE (#$PR)" -f commit_message="$(cat "$MSG")" -f sha=$HEAD_SHA)
23	UUID=$(echo "$R" | jq -r .details.uuid)
24	for i in $(seq 1 30); do r=$(gh api repos/kgang/katalyst/pulls/$PR/merge-async/$UUID); [ "$(echo "$r" | jq -r .status)" != "pending" ] && break; sleep 5; done
25	echo "$r" | jq -c .

66	    seed: int                           # what domain/ will propagate with

70

109	    reason: Literal["reached_terminal", "depth_cap", "width_cap", "claim_cap",
110	                    "spend_cap", "refusal_cap", "no_terminal"]
111	                                        # ONE RULE (proposals.md B4): the reason names what closed the LAST open claim —
112	                                        # an ending or a Stop -> reached_terminal; a cap -> that cap (three refusals in a
113	                                        # row is the refusal cap; it was "model_stopped", but the model did not stop);
114	                                        # spend_cap and no_terminal override
115	                                        # no "search_cap": reaching the search cap stops SEARCHING, not the
116	                                        # generation (later arrows are `argued`), so it is never a stop reason
117	                                        # why the GENERATION stopped. "no_path" is on Verdict only (S3)

126	**The transport is `POST /api/generate` read as a stream, not `EventSource`** (*decided here*). Two reasons, both hard: the request carries a hypothesis, an optional target, an optional user belief and a seed, and `EventSource` can only send a GET with no body; and `EventSource` reconnects by itself, which would silently re-run a generation and spend the money twice. The browser uses `fetch` and reads the body. The wire format is still server-sent events — `event:` and `data:` lines — so the format stays inspectable in a terminal with `curl`.
127	
128	**Four things the cross-chapter review settled (2026-09-17), binding on both stacks.** (1) **A `Stop` and a closed claim make no event of their own.** A `Stop` leaves a transcript line; the next growth event's `frontier` no longer names that claim, and on `beliefs_propagated` **every skeleton goes** — the frontier is empty by definition — so no rectangle ever stands where nothing will arrive. (2) **Which recording plays:** the replayer matches the request's `hypothesis` against each recording's `generation_started.hypothesis`, exact after trimming surrounding spaces; nothing matches → one plain sentence, never a guess. (3) **Readiness says what can be replayed:** `Readiness.replayable: tuple[RecordingSummary, ...]`, `RecordingSummary{example: str, recording_date: date}` — one name, `recording_date`, everywhere. (4) **Anything that is not an accepted proposal counts toward the three in a row** — a validator rejection, a vendor refusal, a malformed answer — one rule, not three.
129	
130	**A recording is this same stream, line for line** — `backend/recordings/<example>.jsonl`, one JSON object per line, in order, with a header line carrying the base map, the seed, the date and the prompt hash (record 0012). On replay every event is re-emitted unchanged **except two (S4)**: `receipt` is **rebuilt** with `mode: "replay"`, zero dollars, and the recording's date and hash; and `beliefs_propagated` is **recomputed** — the recording carries the seed, `domain/` re-propagates, and **a recording therefore holds no `World` at all**, which keeps the file small and makes replay and live agree by construction. Record 0012 names only four event types; the chapter must say all eight and say this.

#!/bin/bash
# heavy.sh <label> -- <command...>
#
# The one queue for anything heavy on this machine: a whole test suite, a browser
# run, a repeat bar. It waits its turn, runs the command, and gives the turn back.
# One at a time, whoever asks. Last session three or four suites ran together, the
# load sat at 20-23, and the load itself caused "flaky" failures that then had to
# be chased (STATUS 2026-09-21).
#
# The turn is a directory (making one is atomic). It holds the owner's process id,
# so a turn left behind by a killed run is taken back rather than waited on for ever.
#
# NOT for a single test file, a linter or a type check: run those directly.
set -uo pipefail
LOCK=/Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst/plans/.heavy.lock
LOG=/Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst/plans/.heavy.log
LABEL=${1:?usage: heavy.sh <label> -- <command...>}; shift
[ "${1:-}" = "--" ] && shift
waited=0
until mkdir "$LOCK" 2>/dev/null; do
  owner=$(cat "$LOCK/pid" 2>/dev/null || echo "")
  if [ -n "$owner" ] && ! kill -0 "$owner" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "heavy: taking back a turn left by dead process $owner ($(cat "$LOCK/label" 2>/dev/null))" >&2
    rm -rf "$LOCK"; continue
  fi
  [ $((waited % 60)) -eq 0 ] && echo "heavy: '$LABEL' waiting behind '$(cat "$LOCK/label" 2>/dev/null)' (${waited}s)" >&2
  sleep 5; waited=$((waited + 5))
done
echo $$ > "$LOCK/pid"; echo "$LABEL" > "$LOCK/label"
trap 'rm -rf "$LOCK"' EXIT
start=$(date +%s)
echo "$(date '+%H:%M:%S') START $LABEL (waited ${waited}s, load $(sysctl -n vm.loadavg | awk '{print $2}'))" >> "$LOG"
"$@"; code=$?
echo "$(date '+%H:%M:%S') END   $LABEL exit=$code took=$(( $(date +%s) - start ))s" >> "$LOG"
exit $code

**Read `/Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst/plans/briefs/04-common.md` first, fully.** It is binding: who Kent is, his two vetoes, the house rules, the report format. This page adds only what is new on 2026-09-21.

## Where the stack stands

Ten pull requests of stack 04 are on `main` (`48eb562`). Four branches remain, each in its own worktree under `/Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst-wt/`. The whole picture is in `/Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst/plans/RESUME-stack-04.md` — read the part about your branch. Kent's instruction for all of it, in his words: *"Aim for a principled but simple as possible project to understand and maintain."* When two designs both work, take the one a stranger could read fastest. Remove rather than guard. One rule over two.

## The machine is shared — the resource rules

Last session three or four agents ran whole suites and 40-times repeat runs together. The load sat at 20–23, everything slowed down, and the load itself caused "flaky" failures that then had to be chased. So:

- **Run directly, as often as you like:** one test file or a few (`uv run pytest tests/unit/domain/test_diff.py`, `npx vitest run src/stream`), the linters, the type checkers, a short script of your own.

- A client library accepting a shape proves nothing about the service.
- Test a program as a program; anything paid for is kept as it goes.

- Never edit a source file under somebody else's running server; never trust an end-to-end number from shared ports.

1	# Midpoint review: finish the reasoning loop and simplify its mathematics
2	
3	**Date:** 2026-09-21. **Status:** recommendation for Kent's review; no product code or accepted decisions changed.
4	
5	## Recommendation
6	
7	Keep the workbench, evidence Inspector, immutable branches, comparison, typed API, and pure domain boundary. Rebuild the quantitative contract around **small explicit models and conditional trade theses**. Finish one complete, keyless Hormuz journey before extending simulation, refinement, probes, or market coverage.
8	
9	The project's central idea fits the assignment well. Its engineering discipline is substantial. The main problem is that the mathematics and feature requirements have grown beyond the evidence supporting them, while the final thesis/strategy experience remains unfinished. Some issues are actual calculation defects, not matters of taste or insufficient disclaimers.
10	
11	Kent's stated priorities during this review were: **no fixed deadline; a compelling, complete demo with defensible assumptions; reconsider the quantitative design from the ground up when it adds apparent certainty rather than useful information.** This proposal follows those priorities. It recommends a bounded redesign, with a specific completion gate, rather than a broad research program.
12	
13	## How the independent review was conducted
14	
15	Four assignment-first passes were frozen before reading the initial brainstorming or existing design. They covered product, probability/causality, finance, and the primary reviewer's synthesis. Each subsequent audit began with `docs/initial-brainstorming.md`, then examined the specs, decisions, implementation, and history. External research used selected primary literature and the assignment's named inspiration sources.
16	
17	Three parallel reviewers used `gpt-5.6-sol`, the available successor to the requested but unavailable `gpt-5-sol`. Their findings were checked and reconciled; the final recommendation below is a synthesis, not a vote or concatenation of reports.
18	
19	The implementation review distinguishes merged `main` (`0df6c23`) from the unmerged browser (`3433266` plus dirty changes), generation (`8261053` plus dirty changes), and observation-fix (`6ee387c` plus a dirty test) worktrees. The newer work already implements much of generation and engine–canvas integration. Recommendations account for it. These are working-tree snapshots, not a claim about the current status of remote pull requests.
20	
21	## What the assignment should make central
22	
23	The brief asks for two entry points into one useful loop:
24	
25	1. Test whether a proposed event plausibly leads to a financial conclusion.
26	2. Discover tradable downstream consequences of an event.
27	
28	Both should lead through **mechanism → evidence → changed scenario → comparison → thesis**. A successful demonstration lets a reviewer explain why the trade looked interesting, what could overturn it, and what the tool still does not know.
29	
30	The brief does not require a universal causal simulator, calibrated forecasts for arbitrary events, daily price paths, portfolio risk, execution, or an ontology framework. Those are possible future directions. They should not determine the first complete product's architecture.
31	
32	## The five highest-leverage adjustments
33	
34	| Priority | Adjustment | Why it earns its cost |
35	|---|---|---|
36	| 1 | Replace the quantitative semantics for the showcase with a bounded, auditable model | Fixes actual probabilistic errors and reduces conceptual machinery |
37	| 2 | Build the conditional thesis and export next, including compatible market comparisons | Completes the assignment and prevents false trade signals |
38	| 3 | Attach evidence to the precise claim or parameter it supports | Makes auditability substantive rather than a count of citations |
39	| 4 | Integrate the existing branches and make one reviewed replay mandatory | Converts substantial unfinished work into a dependable reviewer experience |
40	| 5 | Evaluate semantic quality and time to useful output | Directs future work toward better reasoning and usability, rather than more graph structure |
41	
42	These changes reinforce one another. A smaller model needs fewer parameters to defend, fewer generated claims to research, fewer UI states to explain, and a smaller acceptance suite. The saved effort goes into the thesis and evidence.
43	
44	## Why the numerical reset is warranted
45	
46	### Observation is mathematically wrong in a tiny case
47	
48	Let `P(A)=0.20`, `P(B|A)=0.90`, and `P(B|not A)=0.10`. Observing B should yield `P(A|B)=9/13`, approximately 69%. The current engine returns 20%, unchanged. It selects simulated worlds by their realized outcomes but then averages a conditional probability that is constant for A. The full passing suite does not catch this. The primary reviewer independently reproduced the result.
49	
50	The uncommitted observation test adds another warning sign: it requires movement across a zero-strength arrow, where the declared independent model implies no update. Finite sampling noise has become expected behavior. Details and reproduction: [probability audit](06-probability-audit.md).
51	
52	### The event semantics alter the requested scenario
53	
54	The brief's “Hormuz opens, then Iran is struck” permits both events to occur. A later strike can reduce sustained shipping, increase the risk premium, or reverse the financial conclusion. It does not erase the opening event. Current automatic retraction conflates an event with a continuing state. The implementation can even retract an assumption when a newly inserted opposing source has essentially zero probability, because retraction uses its structural schedule rather than its realized truth.
55	
56	Use distinct dated claims: opening occurred; strike occurred; shipping remains usable through a later date. This makes the story and its arithmetic easier to understand.
57	
58	### Path products and uncertainty bands overstate what is known
59	
60	The Verify path product multiplies dependent marginal probabilities. If Y always equals X and both have probability 0.5, the product is 0.25 while the conjunction is 0.5. The product is neither a general joint probability nor a conservative bound. Remove it.
61	
62	The nested simulation samples a distribution fitted to model-stated probability ranges while holding important parameters and structure fixed. That can explore a declared mathematical distribution, but it does not add evidence. The variance correction does not generally recover its advertised quantiles. A later Brier score on a binary outcome cannot validate an interval over that event's latent probability; the event resolves to true or false, not to its probability.
63	
64	The literature supports distinguishing these objects. Proper scores assess specified predictive quantities; numerical outcome intervals and intervals over unknown probability parameters need different validation designs. [Gneiting and Raftery, 2007](https://doi.org/10.1198/016214506000001437). The audit also identifies mistaken transfers from FermiEval, QuantSightBench, and the forecast-consistency literature into the current ADR rationale.
65	
66	## The proposed quantitative contract
67	
68	**The broad map is a set of causal hypotheses. Quantify a small, complete portion only when doing so helps answer a decision question.**
69	
70	For the showcase, use a small acyclic graph of dated binary claims, normally with at most two direct causes per claim. Record an explicit conditional probability for each parent combination. Compute by exact enumeration at an initial cap near twelve numerical variables. No daily stochastic process, nested Monte Carlo, automatic retraction, or path product is required.
71	
72	The causal interpretation remains an assumption: the selected parents and mechanisms must be adequate for the proposed intervention. Exact arithmetic cannot identify real-world effects from generated text. [Pearl, causal intervention semantics](https://bayes.cs.ucla.edu/BOOK-2K/ch3-3.pdf).
73	
74	Show model-implied probabilities, endpoint changes, and results under a few named coherent assumption sets. The spread across those sets is a sensitivity envelope over what was tested. It has no automatic 80% coverage interpretation. Store user assumptions separately from the model's, and let the user explicitly choose which assumption set a calculation uses; never blend owners silently.
75	
76	An unquantified dependency blocks numerical propagation through it. It may still have a useful mechanism explanation. Reachability tells us which claims may be affected; it does not by itself determine direction or magnitude. Any qualitative change needs an explicit local rule with its conditions, and conflicting or incomplete rules yield ambiguity. Do not hide a model-generated revision behind a deterministic-looking animation.
77	
78	The worked alternative in [09-worked-quantitative-alternative.md](09-worked-quantitative-alternative.md) demonstrates both assignment use cases with four variables. Under its explicitly invented inputs, reopening yields a 55% outcome probability; reopening plus a strike yields 33%. The full pre-event probability is 35%. Its arithmetic was independently checked by enumerating all sixteen joint states.
79	
80	**A table is not automatically better evidence than a log-odds coefficient.** The reason to prefer this design is transparent meaning, exact small-case arithmetic, and lower implementation complexity. If defending the required table entries would force meaningless guesses, keep that endpoint as a conditional scenario/payoff analysis. The model decision experiment has to test this, not assume it away.
81	
82	## Make the thesis financially meaningful
83	
84	The planned “model minus market equals edge” feature is unsafe when the model number assumes the hypothesis is true and the quote spans all possible outcomes. This is a design risk before the thesis stack is implemented, not an allegation that shipped code already calculates this trade signal.
85	
86	In the worked alternative, buying a hypothetical $1 binary payout at $0.40 with $0.02 flat costs loses an expected $0.07 under the full model. Using only the opening scenario would falsely suggest a positive $0.125. If the plan is to enter after opening, use a quote available then; the current quote cannot be assumed to survive the news. Empirical event studies likewise distinguish anticipated information from surprises. [Kuttner, Federal Reserve Bank of New York](https://www.newyorkfed.org/research/staff_reports/sr99.html).
87	
88	The thesis should identify the instrument/exposure, side, horizon, entry condition, current or recorded quote, key assumptions, conditional consequences, and exit logic. Separate:
89	
90	- **Thesis invalidation:** evidence a causal premise failed.
91	- **Offsetting shock:** something else overwhelms the trade while the mechanism remains valid.
92	- **Risk exit:** the user's loss, price, or time rule.
93	- **Execution instruction:** how an order would be submitted and what it can actually guarantee.
94	
95	A sensitivity sweep can suggest monitoring conditions. It cannot derive a guaranteed stop-loss or automatically identify a logical falsifier. Terminal outcomes also cannot establish drawdown or stop-trigger behavior. See the [finance audit](07-finance-audit.md).
96	
97	Use named stresses and conditional losses where calculable. Defer expected shortfall, ruin probabilities, automatic sizing, and portfolio risk until their required position, payoff, path, and distribution inputs exist. Keep “no positive edge at this price” and “conditional thesis; missing quote” as complete, useful results.

They are useful foundations. There is no case here for switching databases, frontend frameworks, or adding services.

110	
111	Source retrieval currently establishes that a URL appeared in the search response. It does not establish that the article supports a probability, timing assumption, effect size, or instrument mapping. Attach a passage or locator, its support role, and the model's explanation of relevance. Verify the trade-critical sources in the showcase by hand. # Digesting the two midpoint reviews — what every digest agent reads first

**You are one of four read-only Opus analysts.** Two independent reviews of the Katalyst project were written on 2026-09-21 by other tools: `plans/review/` (three GPT reviewers and a synthesis) and `plans/review2/` (eight Opus passes and a synthesis; it ran the app and wrote runnable reproductions). Nobody has acted on either. Your job is to digest the part named in your own brief, check it against the code AS IT IS TODAY, and recommend what to do — for the unfinished tail of stack 04 and above all for stacks 05, 06 and 07.

You change NO file in the repository or any worktree and run no git command that changes anything. You write exactly one report, to the path your brief names under `/Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst/plans/analysis/`, plus throwaway scripts under the scratch directory your brief names. Your final message is a 300-word summary of that report.

## What Kent asked for, in his words (2026-09-21)

*"read and digest the critical reviews … and make principled adjustments to the remaining portions, in particular stack 5-7. Rewrites or refactors of the previous stacks are allowed but should be weighed against a high standard of quality improvement. Try to find the best tradeoffs in terms of work required versus improvements made … Aim for a code architecture and design that is principled and simple as possible to understand and maintain."*

So the bar for touching merged work is HIGH, and the currency is improvement per unit of work. A recommendation with no cost beside it is not a recommendation. "Simple" means a stranger reads it fastest: fewer concepts, one rule over two, remove rather than guard.

## Read, in this order

1. `/Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst/ASSIGNMENT.md` — the brief. Everything is judged against it.
2. `/Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst/plans/review2/00-final-proposal.md` and `/Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst/plans/review/00-final-proposal.md` — both recommendations, whole.
3. `/Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst/plans/review2/02-synthesis.md` — what that reviewer verified itself against what it only heard, and its comparison of the two reviews (§7).
4. `/Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst/plans/RESUME-stack-04.md` and the top entry of `/Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst/plans/STATUS.md` — where the project actually stands today.
5. `/Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst/plans/roadmap-03-to-06.md` — the present plan for stacks 05, 06 and 07, which you are revising.
6. `/Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst/AGENTS.md`, `PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md` §3 (decisions), §9 (the fourteen invariants), §10 (anti-patterns), and the decision records under `docs/adr/` that your lens touches.
7. The files your own brief names.

## Facts you must hold on to

- **The reviewers saw an older project.** `review/` read `main` at `0df6c23` plus dirty worktrees; `review2/` read `main` before ten pull requests merged. Today `main` = `48eb562` with #29–#40 merged: the engine–canvas join, the model pipeline, the event stream and replay, two locality fixes (#38), the observe-direction fix (#29). **Every finding must be re-checked against today's code before it counts** — by reading the code, or by a small script. Mark each: STILL TRUE / FIXED SINCE (by what) / PARTLY / NEVER TRUE. Findings that were fixed are worth one line, not a paragraph.
- **The coordinator re-ran review2's two reproductions on today's `main` (48eb562), and BOTH STILL REPRODUCE:** (V1) on a two-claim map A→B, `observe(B=true)` leaves A at exactly `.3000` where Bayes gives `.4562` — identical to `do`; (V2) on Hormuz, supposing C or R true or false (two of B's four causes) moves B by .06–.17 and moves the endings M1 and M2 by `0.0000`; only an edit to B itself moves them. Scripts: `plans/review2/repro/verify_observe.py`, `verify_trigger_read_day.py`, `show_settled_days.py`, `hazard_prototype.py`; run from `/Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst/backend` with `env -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY -u FRED_API_KEY uv run --no-sync python <path>`.
- **Kent has already answered four questions put to him by review2** (question tool, 2026-09-21; recorded in `review2/00-final-proposal.md` and `review2/03-engine-and-finance-design.md`): **an exact core with a sampler on top · keep the time model (trigger/sustain, lag, shapes, half-life) and make it sound · land the open pull requests, then finance before more generation · revisit generation: conditional elicitation, skeleton-first, a small ensemble for numbers.** Treat these as his direction. Your job is to find the cheapest principled way to honour them — and to say plainly where honouring one costs more than it returns, because authority is his and he can only use it on honest numbers.
- **Kent's standing rules still bind**: the two vetoes (a template-looking interface; any state that cannot be traced to an input, a rule or a cited source); every number can say why; model, user and market beliefs are never merged; the model proposes and our code disposes (reject, never repair); `domain/` is pure; no key is ever needed to run the tests or the demo. And, new today: **only the Hormuz example is recorded until he explicitly approves more** — he is concerned about how long paid runs take.
- **Still in flight on stack 04** (do not re-plan these, but say when your findings change one): `fix/04-vanishing-wire`; `feat/04a-growth` (the growing-map screen); `fix/04-payoff-kind-required`; `feat/04b-evals` (evals + a provenance-derived spread on arrow strengths built on the 2 000 × 8 nest + a path product moved into `domain/` — the last is ON HOLD pending your analysis) ; `feat/04b-recordings` (Hormuz only).

## The machine is shared

Other agents are working. Run only light things: a reproduction script, a single test file, a script of your own. **No whole test suites, no playwright, no servers, nothing that calls a model or costs money.** You may read every worktree under `/Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst-wt/`; write in none.

## Your report — the same shape for all four, so they can be laid side by side

1. **The findings table.** One row per distinct finding in your lens, merged across both reviews (say where they agree and where they contradict each other): *finding · who said it · status today (with your evidence: file:line or script output) · what it costs the brief's reader if left · the cheapest honest fix · the fuller fix · cost of each (agent-sessions of roughly three focused hours, and rough lines added / deleted) · verdict.* Verdicts: **NOW** (belongs in the stack-04 tail) · **05** · **06** · **07** · **CUT** (remove the thing rather than fix it) · **REJECT** (the review is wrong or the cost is not worth it — say why).
2. **The design you recommend for your area** — at most 1 200 words, plain words, shapes written as code where a shape is the point. Name what is REMOVED as carefully as what is added. Name which accepted decision records it supersedes or amends.
3. **Where the two reviews disagree, and who is right** — with your reason.
4. **What changes for the branches in flight** — concrete: keep / drop / reorder / rescope, per branch.
5. **Decisions that are genuinely Kent's** — each as he would want it put: plain words, the Hormuz example, what changes on screen and in code, options with the recommended one first and its cost.
6. **What you did not check** — honestly.

48	## 2. The design I recommend
49	
50	### 2.1 The rule that makes the comparison honest
51	
52	> **A model number may be differenced against a market quote only when both range over the same set of worlds — so the edge is computed from the world with *no supposition in force*, and a supposed world can only ever show a conditional payoff.**
53	
54	The smallest shape that enforces it is a **signature, not a guard**. The edge is never computed from "a world"; it is computed by one function that requires the base world as its own argument:
55	
56	```python
57	# katalyst/thesis/edge.py — outside domain/, because it touches a quote (INV-11, ADR-0003)
58	
59	class Quote(BaseModel):                     # what a venue says. Never merged with a model number.
60	    venue: str; contract_id: str
61	    p: float                                # the mid, as a probability
62	    spread: float                           # best offer minus best bid
63	    as_of: date; url: str
64	    source: Literal["fetched", "recorded", "user"]
65	
66	class Edge(BaseModel):                      # built by `priced()` and nowhere else
67	    model: Belief                           # unconditional, owner='model'
68	    quote: Quote
69	    costs: float                            # half the spread plus fees, as a probability
70	    edge: float                             # model.p − quote.p − costs. Signed. May be negative.
71	    break_even: float                       # quote.p + costs — useful even with no quote
72	    mixture: tuple[MixtureTerm, ...]        # every term shown: P(H)·P(c|do H) + (1−P(H))·P(c|do ¬H)
73	
74	class NotComparable(BaseModel):
75	    reason: Literal["conditional_world", "no_quote", "no_contract", "different_question"]
76	    said: str                               # the plain sentence the card prints
77	    break_even: float | None                # still printable when only the quote is missing
78	
79	def priced(base: World, shown: World, claim: PropositionId, quote: Quote | None) -> Edge | NotComparable: ...
80	```
81	
82	`base` and `shown` are two required arguments; there is no way to hand `priced` a branch world alone, and `Edge` has no other construction path. Tests: *agree with the market ⇒ edge reads exactly 0*; *a branch world alone does not type-check*; *a missing quote yields `NotComparable` that still prints the break-even.*
83	
84	The **mixture** is the piece both reviews wanted and neither costed: after *Suppose Hormuz opens*, the card still says *"your supposition makes M1 .61; weighted by the map's own P(H) = .36 against the no-open world's .40, the unconditional number is .47 — that is the one compared with .48."* review/'s worked example, with the engine supplying the terms. It needs only `do(¬A)`, which exists.

86	### 2.2 What a stop-loss honestly is here
87	
88	Four things, kept apart on the card, three of them named differently from today:
89	
90	| Card section | What it is | Who owns it | How it is computed |
91	|---|---|---|---|
92	| **What takes you out** | The events over-represented in the worlds where the stop was touched **first** | computed | `lift(k) = P(k happened before the stop ∣ stop first) / P(k happened)`, Wilson interval on the numerator, suppressed below 200 draws, with the median days between *k* and the stop |
93	| **What to watch** | The claim whose adverse flip hurts the terminal most, **and** resolves before it, **and** is publicly observable | computed | two-directional `sensitivity()` + INV-14's two filters. *Renamed from "invalidation"; it is a watchlist, not a stop.* |
94	| **Your risk exit** | The stop price, the target, the horizon | **the user types them** | never derived |
95	| **Execution** | — | — | We say one sentence: *a stop order's trigger is not its fill price*, and nothing else. |
96	
97	**The smallest thing that is both honest and impressive is "what takes you out".** Forty lines over a boolean mask; the brief's most distinctive sentence answered by computation rather than prose; the one output nobody in the competitive landscape ships. "What to watch" is fifteen lines and is the honest remnant of INV-14. Everything above them — expected shortfall, ruin, drawdown — is cut.
98	
99	**What each needs from the engine.** Only one thing, and it is small:
100	
101	```python
102	# katalyst/thesis/draws.py — the ONLY coupling between the finance layer and the engine
103	class Draws(BaseModel):
104	    day_zero: date; days: int
105	    order: tuple[PropositionId, ...]
106	    when:   NDArray[int]      # (n, claims): the day each claim first became true, −1 for never
107	    weight: NDArray[float]    # (n,): all ones for an exact ancestral sampler
108	```
109	
110	"What to watch" needs **endpoint marginals only** — today's `sensitivity()` gives them. P(stop first) / P(target first) need **event times per world**. The inverse query needs **joint samples with times**. All three come from `when`.
111	
112	`weight` is in the shape from day one so the finance layer is **indifferent to ENGINE's Plan A versus Plan B**: an exact core with an ancestral sampler gives weights of one, a likelihood-weighted sampler gives real weights, and nothing above changes. And `when` is derivable from *today's* engine too — `_draw` already computes `truth[claim] = came_true`, a `(versions, worlds, days)` boolean array, whose first true day **is** `when`. **So stack 05 is not blocked on the engine reformulation**: write it against synthetic `Draws`, test it against synthetic `Draws`, turn it on over whichever engine lands.

## A′. The two pre-existing defects the coordinator asked about (not fixed, on main too)

Both reproduce **unchanged** on this branch, so the spread neither creates nor masks either.

**1. `observe(B=true)` leaves a cause at its prior (.3000 against Bayes's .4562).** Root cause: step 3 of `propagation.md` B5 — *keep the likelihood, not the coin flip*. `_one_pass` keeps `answer` (the claim's marginal likelihood in that draw) and throws away `came_true` (the realised flag). For a claim with **no causes** `total` is `broadcast(baseline)`, so `answer` is *identical in all eight worlds of a version*; `_per_version` then averages it over the surviving subset and gets exactly the same number back. Rao-Blackwellisation is exact for an *unconditional* mean, and invalid once you condition on another claim's realised outcome, because the conditioning event depends on the value that was discarded. The Bayes answer would come back by reading `came_true[A]` over the surviving worlds instead of `answer[A]`, at the cost of the variance reduction the whole band rests on — which is why this is a design decision and not a patch. It is the same phenomenon `diff.md` already records as G3's "moved only by reweighting", described there as a property rather than as a defect. **Interaction with the spread: none.** A has no incoming arrows, so no drawn push enters its baseline and its answer is still constant across worlds within a version. For a claim that *does* have causes, the answer already varies across worlds, the observation does reach it, and the spread only widens the band.

**2. `do(C)`/`do(R)` move B but move M1 and M2 by exactly 0.0000.** Root cause: `fired[claim_id] = came_true[:, :, starts]` where `starts = _point_of(points, setup.settled[claim_id])`. A **trigger** arrow multiplies its push by that single flag — the source's truth on the source's own *settled* day — while a **sustain** arrow multiplies by the full per-day `truth` array. `settled[B]` is day 2, the day B's *earliest* live arrow (`H→B`, lag 2) reaches it; `C→B` has lag 7 and `R→B` lag 5, so their pushes land in B's own series (B goes `.393 → .476` under `do(C)`) and are invisible to `B→M1` and `B→M2`. The intent in the code comment is defensible — a claim must be true-or-false once per world, or a sustaining push would flicker day to day — but the day chosen is a property of the map's *earliest* arrow rather than of when the trigger fires. The two readings that would let later pushes through are "the day this arrow's own push fires" (`settled[source] + lag`) and "the source's own resolve-by day"; both change every recorded number, so this is Kent's call. **Interaction with the spread: none that can change the zero.** The spread varies `H→B`, `C→B` and `R→B`, so it changes the distribution of B's day-2 flag — but identically in the base world and the `do(C)` world, because C's arrow contributes nothing on day 2 in either. The base-versus-branch difference stays exactly zero, which I confirmed by running the repro here.

135	   with the clause that qualifies it. ~80 lines.

137	   silhouette already marks that tile; where the three belief columns sit, a tile carrying a
138	   position draws a p10/p50/p90 strip with the stop and target as two vertical rules. This
139	   is where C21 pays: collapsing `user`/`market` to glyphs frees exactly this room, and it
140	   makes the tradeable tile *look different*, which is what a reader should see. ~150 lines,
141	   `roomFor` gains one case.

143	   region with the whole card, map still beside it. Nothing opens over anything. ~150 lines,
144	   mostly re-rendering sections that exist.

147	columns on unselected tiles (C21); `.branch-panel`'s two dead scroll rules (C3); the rail's
148	methodology note, to below its rows (C4); the origin strip's routes, seed and loop counts, to

151	**What is NOT added:** no tab bar, no dialog, no drawer, no second panel, no minimap, no

154	section or a strip in the existing frame; every new control is a word with a hairline round

194	
195	Weighed on its merits, as asked. The drift is real: **260 distinct numeric literals, 1,162
196	occurrences, 33 files.** The strict rule would delete ~100 passages that currently *teach* —
197	a chapter saying "B's band is 30 points wide and 65 % of it is B's own prior" is teaching what

200	So: **one owning place, generated, checked in CI; chapters quote and link.**
201	
202	- `make numbers` runs the engine on Hormuz at seed `20261001` and writes
203	  `spec/graph/hormuz-numbers.md`: every claim's `p (lo–hi)`, the strike branch's before/after
204	  per ending, agreement shares, band shares, with a header naming what produced it.
205	- A test regenerates it and fails on a diff. **Exactly the mechanism `types-fresh` already
206	  uses and the project already trusts.**
207	- The rule becomes: *a number the engine computes appears in prose only where the owning
208	  table is one link away, and that table is generated.*
209	- The golden test **cannot** serve this purpose and should not be asked to:
210	  `test_hormuz_golden.py` pins *directions, orderings and named states — never values*, on
211	  purpose, because the fixture's inputs are tuned. That is the right design; it just means
212	  the owning table has to be new.
213	- **The strict rule applies to `docs/adr/` alone.** A record is immutable; a number inside one
214	  is wrong for ever. ADR-0014 carries 76 numeric literals today.
215	- **What this also fixes:** the inventory separates *inputs* (priors, strengths, lags, dates —
216	  authored in `fixtures/hormuz.py`, stable, safe to quote) from *engine-computed* marginals.
217	  Nobody has been making that distinction, and it is why sweeps have been touching numbers
218	  that never needed touching.

241	
242	**Keep, emphatically:** the read-only reviewer before every pull request. It is the cheapest
243	quality mechanism in the project and it keeps catching real defects — RW found that the wire
244	fix's hook polls for ever (a must-fix); the growth branch was reviewed twice and each round
245	produced must-fixes with tests that failed first.

247	**ADR-0009 holds five rules and only one is expensive.** Conventional commits, branch naming,
248	the three pull-request headings, squash-merge and always-green all cost nothing and are

250	one is *"the bottom pull request is docs-only and merges first … never deeper than four"*,
251	because it makes the order of merging a constraint on the order of thinking, and the bottom —
252	the docs PR — is the thing most likely to move. The measured cost was a three-case rebase
253	recipe with a proof obligation, seven hand-maintained "coordinator owes" queues, a
254	file-ownership table, an event vocabulary mirrored by hand in two languages, and four days
255	with `main` static.

260	> headings, the squash-merge and the always-green rule are unchanged. `land.sh` stays for the
261	> two-deep case; the async-merge endpoint is retired.

269	writing prose about the same subject.**

104	
105	### What a claim means
106	
107	A claim is a resolvable proposition with a deadline `D`, and its number is
108	`P(it resolves YES by D)` — a first-passage probability, which is what the sentence on the
109	tile already says. It is not an instantaneous state probability read on a deadline, and it
110	can never un-resolve.
111	
112	### Where the time model lives
113	
114	On the edge, unchanged in vocabulary. Every arrow keeps `strength`, `mode`, `lag`, `shape`,
115	`half_life`; they now modify a **hazard** — the rate at which a claim happens on a given day —
116	instead of a log-odds read on one day:
117	
118	```
119	λ_i(t) = λ⁰_i · exp( Σ_j  w_ij · shape_ij(t − τ_j − lag_ij) )
120	P(i by D_i | parents) = 1 − exp( −∫₀^{D_i} λ_i(t) dt )
121	```
122	
123	`λ⁰` comes from the claim's own `prior`, which is honestly the leak — `q₀ = P(i by D | no
124	modelled cause)` — and the edge weight from `q₁ = P(i by D | this cause happened)`, both in
125	closed form (review2 `03` §1.3). The integral is exact per piecewise-constant segment, so it
126	is grid-independent **provided every breakpoint is on the grid** — which is exactly what
127	`_prepare`'s `must_be_exact` set already guarantees, and it is what keeps the #38 locality
128	proof alive. An impulse's whole area now counts, so the answer no longer depends on where
129	the deadline falls relative to the half-life; that is E5 and ADR-0014's admitted wart, gone.
130	
131	### Where the parent's arrival time comes from
132	
133	**One forward pass, not inference.** Each claim's own first-passage distribution over a
134	coarse grid (K ≈ 12–24 epochs) is computed once, causes first, in `O(n·K·2^indegree)`; a
135	`do` recomputes it with that claim pinned to the day it was supposed. A child's conditional
136	table is then the hazard integral averaged over its parents' arrival distributions.
137	
138	That is the entire idea, and it is the one thing neither review proposed. Measured cost of
139	the approximation against full exact inference over event times: **worst 0.0065** on a
140	multi-parent map, **97 % of all numbers within 0.01** over 30 generated maps with inhibitors.
141	Measured saving: **0.5 ms against 0.7–7.8 s** for a 20-claim band.
142	
143	### What solves the network
144	
145	The claims are then **binary**, and the joint is solved **exactly** by variable elimination
146	with a min-fill ordering — the 200 parameter versions and the ~180 displayed days carried as
147	leading `numpy` axes, so the whole band is one pass. `do` replaces a factor with a point mass
148	and cuts the arrows in; `observe` multiplies in an indicator and renormalises. Both are
149	exact, which kills E1, E3, E4 and E9 in one change. The band becomes the 10th/90th percentile
150	of 200 exact answers — ADR-0014's *meaning* of the range is untouched; its machinery shrinks
151	to a loop.
152	
153	Two properties fall out rather than being engineered. **Locality becomes a theorem**: a
154	claim d-separated from the evidence gets its prior back bit-for-bit, because its factor sums
155	to one — so `_observation_reach`'s careful per-observation masks stop being a mechanism and
156	become a fact. And **`range_shares` becomes exact**: re-solve with one prior frozen, `n`
157	extra solves at 0.5 ms, instead of a 20-bin estimator over a discarded sample.
158	
159	### Worlds still exist, and the finance layer still gets event times
160	
161	Draw worlds by sampling truths from the exact joint, then sampling each true claim's arrival
162	day forward. No inference over times is ever needed, because nothing conditions on a time.
163	That is what feeds the price paths, the first-touch stop/target computation and the
164	lift-based inverse query in review2 `03` §2 — so **the time model still earns its keep in
165	exactly the place review2 says it does**, at none of Plan A's cost.
166	
167	### What is REMOVED

169	The 2 000 × 8 nested loop. Rejection sampling. The noise correction `f` and every clamp in
170	it. `inner_spread`, `_per_version`, `_surviving_both`, the version weights, `LOWEST_SURVIVAL`
171	and the starvation warning. The per-claim uniforms (`coins`) and the `WORLDS_STREAM`. The

173	double duty. The path product and the stored `p = 1.0` on a supposed claim whose only reader
174	it is.
175

178	Branches-as-patches and `apply`. `validity.py` and its 13 codes. The affected set and the

200	## 3. The four options, honestly costed
201	
202	### (a) Minimal repair inside today's engine
203	
204	**Root causes, found.** V1: `propagation.py:1470-1472` — `_per_version(answer, …)` averages
205	the Rao–Blackwellised conditional `p(claim | parents)` over surviving worlds. That estimator
206	is exact only when no evidence node is a descendant of the claim; for an ancestor it returns
207	a constant. V2: `_settled_days` at `propagation.py:806-843`, line 842 `min(arrivals)`,
208	consumed at `:1446` and `:1463` — one integer does two different jobs, "when do this claim's
209	outgoing delays start counting" and "on which day is this claim's truth decided".
210	
211	**Can V1 be fixed by weighting worlds properly rather than versions?** Partly, and it breaks
212	something else. Replace rejection with likelihood weighting and estimate from the sampled
213	truth flags (not `answer`) for claims with evidence among their descendants — ~30 lines, and
214	the headline `p` becomes unbiased with a standard error of ~0.006 at the shipped budget.
215	**But the band dies.** The within-version variance of a Bernoulli flag is ≈ 0.25 against an
216	across-version variance of ≈ 0.01, so `f = √(max(0, 1 − within/across))` clamps to **zero**
217	and every band under `observe` collapses to a point — reporting certainty where there is
218	none. Fixing that means raising `worlds` by ~30× (66 ms → ~2 s per call) or abandoning the
219	noise correction. So V1's minimal repair costs either the band or the latency.
220	
221	**Can V2 be fixed by reading the cause on the right day?** Not cheaply. The right day is
222	per world, so `shape_rows` becomes a `(versions, worlds, days)` array per arrow and `settled`
223	becomes random — and `settled` is what the grid, `_states`, `_spells_on`, the retraction
224	schedule and the #38 locality proof are all built on. Integrating over *when* the cause
225	happened is not a repair; it is the reformulation.
226	
227	**Cost:** 1.5 sessions, +120 / −60, and it leaves standing: the path products, the meaning of
228	the band under `observe`, the clamp bias, zero-survivor versions, retraction by schedule, the
229	claims-un-resolve copula, `prior`-as-leak, and the fact that `p` is an instantaneous read for
230	a proposition phrased "by". **Verdict: REJECT as the destination.** Two of its pieces are
231	worth doing *now* as insurance in case §2 slips: the per-version effective-sample-size warning
232	(E3) and the survivor-count divisor (E4), 17 lines together.

234	### (b) review2's Plan A — hazard first-passage network, exact VE over event times
235	
236	I ran `hazard_prototype.py`. It is correct and it is honest: the calibration reproduces the
237	elicited `q₀`/`q₁` to four places, the grid invariance is real (K=6 `.4239` → K=240 `.4374`),
238	`do(A)` reaches the grandchild, `observe(B)` gives exact Bayes upstream, and the forward
239	sampler agrees with the exact answer inside 3 standard errors. Every idea of ADR-0005
240	survives with its meaning intact. **The model is right and I am adopting it.**
241	
242	The inference is not. The prototype builds a dense joint over three variables; §1.5 asserts
243	that variable elimination scales this to 15–30 claims at `K ≈ 12–16`. Measured, it does not
244	(E16). Its own kill criterion — "a generated 30-claim map exceeds ~1 s" — fires at K=6, before
245	the grid is even fine enough to state a tolerance.
246	
247	There is a second, quieter cost. Under first-passage semantics τ is absorbing, so a `sustain`
248	edge from an event source is **identical** to a `trigger` edge. Plan A therefore dissolves the
249	project's most original idea unless the event/state split (§1.4) is also taken — and a state
250	claim needs two times, on and off, which squares its factor. §1.4 says the split is optional;
251	for `sustain` it is not.

256	at the grid you intend to ship, stop.* It is 1.7–19.6 ms at K=12 today. **Verdict: adopt the
257	model, REJECT the inference.**

261	Measured on a 20-claim map: 3.5 ms at 2 000×8 (s.e. 0.0058), 10.5 ms at 200×250 (s.e. 0.0034),

# Design after the midpoint reviews — what changes, what stays, and why

**2026-09-21 · coordinator's synthesis · PROPOSED.** Nothing here is accepted until Kent accepts the decision records it names (`AGENTS.md`: nothing is built against a `proposed` record). The plan that executes it is `PLAN.md`. The questions that are genuinely Kent's are in `notes/2026-09-21-decisions-after-review.md`.

**Where it comes from.** Two independent reviews (`review/`, `review2/`) were digested by four read-only Opus analysts, each of whom re-checked every finding against today's code (`main` = `48eb562`): `analysis/2026-09-21-digest-{engine,finance,generation,craft}.md`. Those four reports hold the evidence — file and line, scripts, measurements. This page holds the conclusions and settles the places where the analysts disagreed. Kent's four answers to `review2` (2026-09-21) are treated as direction: **an exact core with a sampler on top · keep the time model and make it sound · land what is open, then finance before more generation · revisit generation.**

**The bar** (Kent, 2026-09-21): rewrites of merged work are allowed *"but should be weighed against a high standard of quality improvement … the best tradeoffs in terms of work required versus improvements made."* And: the spec stays a first-class book; shorten it *where warranted*, not as a maxim.

---

## 1. The verdict in six lines

1. **The foundations stand.** Branches as patches, the validator that rejects and never repairs, locality, the typed wire, replay, the canvas and its keyboard: both reviews and all four analysts say keep them. Nothing here is a rewrite of the product.
2. **The arithmetic does not.** Three defects reproduce on today's `main`, on the demo map, under 100% coverage: *This happened* never updates a cause; two of Brent's four causes move nothing downstream; a claim nobody believes can void the reader's own supposition. **No test compares the engine with an independently computed answer** — that one absence let all three through.
3. **The fix is smaller than either review thought.** Keep `review2`'s time model exactly; stop solving for *when*; solve *whether* exactly. Half a millisecond for a whole band on a 20-claim map, against seconds for `review2`'s own plan. Net **fewer** lines in `propagation.py`.
4. **The brief ends in a trade and the trade has no code.** Stack 06 builds it in four pull requests, with one narrow contract to the engine so it does not wait for the engine work to finish.
5. **Every change to what we ask the model for lands once**, then Hormuz is recorded once. The payoff `kind` fix waits for that.
6. **Less is built, on purpose.** Cut: the path product, `refine`, feedback-loop unrolling, the simulation probe, the pastcast, expected shortfall and ruin, a fifth kind of claim, a probability slider, screenshot baselines.

---

## 2. The engine — what a number means, and how it is worked out

### 2.1 The three defects (all on `main` today, all re-run)

| | What happens | Root cause |
|---|---|---|
| **An observation never reaches a cause.** | Two claims, A → B. *This happened* on B leaves A at `.3000`; the right answer is `.4562`. It prints the same number as *Suppose this is true*. | The engine keeps each claim's worked-out likelihood and throws away the coin flip. For a claim with no causes that likelihood is the same in every world, so filtering worlds by the observation cannot move it (`propagation.py:1470`). |
| **Endings are deaf to half their causes.** | On Hormuz, supposing the insurance premium (C) or OPEC+ restraint (R) moves Brent (B) by .06–.17 and moves both endings by `0.0000`. | A trigger arrow reads its source on the day the source's **earliest** incoming arrow lands. For B that is day 2; C's push lands on day 7 and R's on day 5 — inside B's own series, invisible to B's outgoing arrows (`propagation.py:806-843`, `:1463`). |
| **A claim nobody believes deletes a supposition.** | Insert a claim with a prior of `.001` and an arrow of `−0.01` into a supposed claim: the tile never reads *Supposed*, on any day. | A supposition ends on a calendar worked out from the map's shape. It never asks whether the opposing cause happened, or how hard it pushes (`propagation.py:888-948`). |

Also true: the range under an observation can be made entirely of coin flips (`.157` wide with every input frozen); a merged test (`test_an_observation_moves_a_cause_even_when_no_arrow_pushes`) enshrines sampling noise as required behaviour.

### 2.2 The design — proposed record 0016

**A claim's number is the chance it resolves YES by its own deadline.** That is what the sentence on the tile already says. It is not a snapshot read on one day, and a claim that has happened never un-happens.

**The time model stays, on the arrow, word for word.** `strength`, `mode`, `lag`, `shape`, `half_life` keep their meanings. They now bend a *rate* — how likely the claim is to happen on each day — rather than a likelihood read on one day. The claim's number is that rate added up over its window. An impulse's whole area counts, so the answer no longer depends on where a deadline falls against a half-life (record 0014's admitted wart goes).

**When a cause arrives comes from one forward pass, not from inference.** Causes first, each claim's chance of having happened by each of 12–24 points in its window; a *Suppose* pins its claim to its day and the pass is redone. A child's table is then its rate averaged over when its causes arrived.

**Whether each claim happens is then solved exactly** — the standard method for a sparse network of yes/no claims (variable elimination: multiply the small tables together and sum out one claim at a time, cheapest first). *Suppose* replaces a table with a certainty and cuts the arrows in. *This happened* multiplies in the evidence and renormalises. Both exact. All 200 versions and every displayed day ride along as array axes, so a whole band is one pass.

**Measured** (analyst's scripts, `scratchpad/digest/engine/`):

| 20 claims, up to 3 causes each | one band |
|---|---|
| `review2`'s plan — exact over event *times*, 12 points | **0.7–7.8 s**, up to 63 million table entries; 58–119 s at 30 claims |
| this design — exact over *truths*, timing from the forward pass | **0.5 ms**; 1.7 ms at 30 claims |
| what the shortcut costs in accuracy, against the exact-over-times answer | worst **.0065** on a multi-parent map; over 30 generated maps, 97% of numbers within .01 |

**What falls out rather than being engineered:** locality becomes a theorem (a claim cut off from the evidence gets its own table back, bit for bit); the range becomes exact — the 10th and 90th percentile of 200 exact answers, record 0014's *meaning* untouched; *same direction* measures the model, not the dice; "which input explains this range" becomes one extra exact solve.

**Worlds still exist.** Draw whether each claim happens from the exact answer, then draw *when*, forward. That sample is what the trade needs (§3). Nothing ever conditions on a time, so nothing needs inference over times.

**Removed:** the 2 000 × 8 nest, rejection sampling, the noise correction and its clamps, version weights, the low-survival warning, the per-claim coins, the settled-day's double duty, `moved_only_by_reweighting` (there is no reweighting). About **−1 100 / +750** in `propagation.py`. **Kept untouched:** `apply` and branches, `validity.py`, the affected set, `Diff`'s states and the ranked list, and the `World` and `Diff` shapes the browser reads (15 900 lines stand on them).

**The first thing written is the test that was missing:** a brute-force oracle over generated maps of five claims or fewer, forbidden from importing the engine's internals (the way the locality oracle may not call `affected_set`), asserting every number under no edit, *Suppose*, and *This happened*. It fails today. It grades both engines. Tolerance: three standard errors against the sampler, `1e-9` against the exact core.

**Staged so `main` is never red and the canvas never shows nonsense:** oracle (expected failures marked strict) → new core beside the old behind a flag, default unchanged → one flip that changes every number once, with one reviewable diff of exactly which (§6).

### 2.3 Three things that ride with it

- **The path product goes (proposed; rewrites INV-8 and FR-11 — Kent's).** Multiplying likelihoods along a route is not the chance of anything when claims share causes (if Y always equals X and both are .5, the product says .25 and the truth is .5). It was never moved into `domain/`; that item is dropped. Replacement, once the exact core exists — three real quantities, one or two extra solves each: the **shift** the hypothesis makes to the destination (`P(dest | suppose true) − P(dest | suppose false)`); the **chance every step on the route goes right**, as a true joint; and **which single arrow carries most of the shift**. The trade needs the first one anyway.
- **Event and state (proposed record 0017 — reverses part of record 0014, Kent's).** *"Hormuz opens, then Iran is struck"* should leave both standing. A claim gains `persistence: event | state`; an event, once it happened, happened; a state can stop holding; a `sustain` arrow may only leave a state. Hormuz gains one claim — *the strait stays open to commercial transit through 1 November* — which the opening causes and the strike inhibits. Automatic retraction is **deleted**: about −250 server lines, −120 browser, +60. *Open point for the red team: under "happens by its deadline" a `sustain` arrow out of an event is indistinguishable from a trigger — so this split may be required by §2.2, not optional.* The fallback if Kent declines: date a retraction from whether the opposing cause actually happened, per world (+40 lines); it fixes the third defect and not the brief's sentence.
- **The provenance spread lands now.** It draws one strength per arrow per *version*, and versions are the part of today's engine the new core keeps. Its visible effect on the scripted strike — B and N1 read `unchanged`; N1, the biggest mover, because its one arrow is the map's one bare assertion — is the product telling the truth, and the new `unchanged_because: versions_disagree` says so in words. Kent sees it at M4.

### 2.4 Settled between analysts

- **Formatting stays in `domain/`.** One analyst wanted it moved to the browser (one session); the engine analyst measured it at 31 executable lines, tested against its browser twin. Not worth it. Fix the three places that print a raw float into text a reader sees (~10 lines). Revisit only if Kent chooses `36%` over `.36` — then moving it first makes that a one-file change.
- **Do not split `propagation.py`.** 812 lines of code under long docstrings, and §2.2 rewrites most of it.

---

## 3. The trade — stack 06, on open ground

Full design: `analysis/2026-09-21-digest-finance.md` §2. The load-bearing choices:

**Like with like (proposed record 0018).** A model number may be set against a market quote only when both range over the same worlds. So an edge is computed from the world with **no supposition in force**, and the shape enforces it — one function, `priced(base, shown, claim, quote) -> Edge | NotComparable`, with no signature that takes a branch world alone. After *Suppose Hormuz opens* the card still reaches an honest number by showing the mixture term by term: *P(H) × the supposed reading + (1 − P(H)) × the reading with H supposed false*. With no quote it prints a **break-even** anyway — the most useful thing to say when there is nothing to compare.

**A stop is a price the reader owns (proposed record 0019; amends INV-14, FR-23, FR-24).** The roadmap's derived stop-loss yields nothing usable on its own fixture — the only claim resolving before the Brent ending is the thing the thesis bets on — and the sweep only ever flips claims one way. Four things kept apart on the card: **what takes you out** (computed: which events are over-represented in the worlds where the stop is touched first); **what to watch** (computed: the adverse flip that hurts most, resolves earlier, and can be observed — the honest remnant of INV-14); **your exit** (stop, target, horizon — typed by the reader, never derived); **execution** (one sentence: a stop's trigger is not its fill).

**One contract with the engine**, so the two stacks do not wait on each other:

```python
class Draws(BaseModel):            # thesis/draws.py — the ONLY coupling to the engine
    day_zero: date; days: int
    order: tuple[PropositionId, ...]
    when:   NDArray[int]           # (n, claims): the day each claim first came true, −1 for never
    weight: NDArray[float]         # (n,): all ones from an exact sampler
```

**Not built:** a fifth, price-valued kind of claim (a position already holds spot, volatility and horizon, none of which a model can supply — and the new kind would cost a validity rule, a prompt change and a paid re-recording); two-sided payoffs (the loss leg *is* the stop); expected shortfall, drawdown, ruin, portfolio risk, automatic sizing; Kalshi; an event-study helper.

**Outside data with no key (proposed record 0020; amends 0010).** Quotes are recorded first and fetched second: a committed dated file the demo and the build run on; an opt-in live Polymarket read that falls back to it; a reader-entered quote always available. A FRED figure is a measured level — a spot anchor with its attribution line — never a `market` belief. On screen a quote is never a bare number: `Polymarket · .48 · recorded 2026-09-21`.

**The export** is `legs[] + conditions[]`, never an order format, and carries its own limits **as data** (`refuses: [...]`, `not_advice`), so an agent that ingests it ingests the caveats. There is no "not investment advice" line anywhere in the repository today.

**The fixture contradicts itself today:** the prose says model `.61` against market `.48`, "13 points of edge"; the engine says `.456`, so the flagship trade is a *sell* by accident, in five files. Deleted with the number rule (§6); the fixture's six honest fixes ride with stack 06.

**On screen** (craft analyst §2): no new real estate. One pinned three-line **YOUR TRADE** strip above the panel's scroll — the only pinned thing in the product; *what takes you out* and *what carries it* are the existing change-list component run on a different question; the outcome strip draws on the tradeable tile, which is why unselected tiles first collapse their two empty belief columns to a glyph row; the card is a state of the panel, never a dialog.

---

## 4. Generation — settle the shapes once, buy speed cheaply, bet later

Measured on the committed recording and three kept runs (generation analyst §0) — several of `review2`'s claims are already out of date:

- **The map is not a tree.** 1.12–1.37 arrows per claim, claims with two and four causes, `LinkProposal` used in 2 of 20 and 7 of 28 accepted proposals. The *quality* case for drafting a whole map in one call is gone; its remaining case is speed, and against measured $0.139 and 55 tokens a second a call, `review2`'s "3 minutes, $0.70" is about 2× optimistic on time and 3× on money.
- **Search is the clock.** A call that searches takes 3–4× the seconds. 93 searches bought five base rates on eighteen claims; three of the five are `0/2`, `2/3`, `1/1`.
- **The map has no arrow that pushes down because the prompt never asks.** The words are not in it. The scripted insert, which *is* adversarial, drew three negative arrows unprompted.
- **`review2`'s evidence check cannot be built** — the search tool returns encrypted content and the structured answer carries no citations. `review/`'s version can: a quoted passage and the role it plays.

**One shape freeze (stack 05), then one paid re-record of Hormuz.** Everything that changes the standing prompt or the answer shapes moves the prompt fingerprint and makes the recording stale, so they go in together:

```python
class LinkDraft(BaseModel):
    mode: Literal["trigger", "sustain"]
    p_effect_if_cause: float          # "how likely is the effect if the cause happens?"
    p_effect_if_not_cause: float      # "…and if it does not?"  — our code derives the arrow's weight
    lag: int; shape: Literal["impulse", "step", "ramp"]; half_life: int | None
    rationale: str
    what_would_change_my_mind: str    # one named observable
    sources: tuple[SourceDraft, ...]

class SourceDraft(BaseModel):
    url: str
    quote: str                        # the sentence on that page that carries the weight
    role: Literal["mechanism", "magnitude", "timing", "resolution", "instrument"]
```

…plus `kind` required on both payoffs (**the branch already written — held until the freeze**); a price ending's expected `move` as a range (it rides free here; added later it is a second paid re-record); three sentences asking for what would *stop* each step and what would *falsify* each ending; no search on the first call (7 s to a first tile, measured) and five claims at once; research a base rate only where a reference class can exist, and drop a count under five; a rule that a price ending's instrument appears in its own test. Removed: the elicited `strength`, and with it the anchor "+1 triples the odds" — a number we wrote inside a prompt. Free check that comes with it: the model's three numbers round an arrow must roughly agree, and the Inspector can show by how much they do not. Amends records 0006, 0010, 0013; record 0015 stands.

**The existing `hormuz.jsonl` is valid against `main` and lands as it is.** The payoff defect is latent — the model filled the field in all eleven trades.

**Later, gated (stack 07):** drafting a skeleton in one streamed call is a bet with a kill switch on the scorecard, not a premise; a small ensemble only if the scorecard earns it; fetching a cited page ourselves to check the quote. **Kept untouched:** three silent retries; one walk-driver; every refusal an event; provenance decided by us.

---

## 5. The screen

`review2`'s interface audit ran an older branch. On `feat/04a-growth` today six of its findings are fixed (one scrolling panel with measured edge marks; `App.tsx` 1 524 → 483 lines; the view framed to the stage; a memoised engine state; an error boundary; a light theme). **Still true and demo-deciding: the brief's core interaction has no mouse route** — the six operations open from `e` or the palette only. A **polish pull request** (one session, browser only, after growth lands) carries that button and eight small things a reviewer meets in the first two minutes; its end-to-end check is *geometric* — every control inside the panel's box at 1440 × 900 and 1280 × 800 — never a pixel baseline.

Rejected with reasons: a probability slider (every edit appends to an audit trail with no undo — scrubbing writes thirty edits, or opens a second unaudited path; *Change this push* already is the honest version); small multiples; merging the PRD and `ARCHITECTURE.md` (merging does not fix drift — a 40-line test of its **built**/**planned** markers does); a reducer for `MapScreen`.

---

## 6. Documents and process — targeted, not a freeze

- **One owning place for the worked example's numbers.** `make numbers` runs the engine on Hormuz and writes one committed file; the build regenerates it and fails on a difference — the `types-fresh` pattern, already trusted. Chapters may quote and link. When the engine core flips, *the diff of that one file is the complete statement of every number that moved.* A lint (a decimal in prose must appear in that file or on a short allow-list) arrives with the engine stack's sweep. Today: about 90 engine-computed numbers in 13 files, 547 decimals in all, and a README whose `curl` example prints 16 digits a reader will not get.
- **Eight local cuts to the spec, about 17%, none a freeze** (craft analyst §3): cite the visual checklist by stable name (35 citations by line number today; it has thirteen lines and `ARCHITECTURE.md` says twelve); fold answered open questions into the chapter that owns them (52 of 100 are answered in place); move dated history out of behaviour sections into the records; **change one line of the chapter template** — a *Data model* section gives the shape and names the module, not the class body (that one line accounts for ~43 000 words, 50–79% identical to the code); one owner per repeated rule. Each rides in the pull request that touches the chapter; none is a sweep of its own.
- **About twenty workbench passages still say "in this stack there is no engine"** — true of stack 03b. The largest untruth left in the book; one agent, one pass.
- **Process (proposed amendment to record 0009 — Kent's):** a stack is at most **two** deep. Kept: Conventional Commits, branch names, the three headings, squash-merge, always green, and **a read-only reviewer before every pull request** (it found a must-fix on every branch this stack). The rule the evidence supports for agents is not a head-count: **one agent per file-owning area; never two agents writing prose about one subject.** Whole suites and browser runs go through one queue (`scripts/heavy.sh`); only the coordinator runs playwright, repeat bars, or anything paid.

---

## 7. What is not being done, and why

| Cut | Why |
|---|---|
| The path product | Not a probability of anything when claims share causes |
| `refine` and INV-10; feedback-loop unrolling; the random-simulation probe | Nothing in the brief asks; research projects over an exact core. INV-10 is met by a named refusal, and the definition of done says so |
| The pastcast | Needs evidence frozen before each event, which the pipeline does not have; one resolved event is not a track record. One honest sentence on the "what I would do next" page |
| Expected shortfall, drawdown, ruin, automatic sizing | Need a capital base and a portfolio; theatre without them |
| A price-valued fifth kind of claim; two-sided payoffs | A position already holds those numbers; the loss leg is the stop |
| Exact inference over event times; full tables per parent combination; enumeration | Measured too slow, or 2^k numbers a model states incoherently |
| Freezing `spec/`; merging PRD and `ARCHITECTURE.md`; moving formatting out of `domain/`; splitting `propagation.py` | Kent's correction; or the cost does not clear the bar |
| A probability slider, small multiples, screenshot baselines, a wall-clock gate in the build | An unaudited edit path; a dashboard; two flake generators |
| The other three recordings | Kent, 2026-09-21: Hormuz only until he explicitly approves |

# PLAN — from here to a finished prototype

**2026-09-21 · PROPOSED until Kent answers `notes/2026-09-21-decisions-after-review.md`.** Replaces `roadmap-03-to-06.md` (kept under History for its ticked boxes). The reasons are in `design-after-midpoint-review.md`; the evidence is in `analysis/2026-09-21-digest-*.md`. A session below is about three focused hours of one agent.

**The shape of what is left:** finish stack 04 (small) → **05 sound numbers** → **06 the trade** → **07 a map you can argue with, shown to be good**. Stacks 05 and 06 overlap in time; their files are disjoint.
